- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33) and forecast is overly optimistic, shift downward by 3–5% to align with bearish sentiment.  
- After a recent price spike, model tends to overreact — apply a 2–3 day lag correction by lowering forecast 1–2% per day until trend stabilizes.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 2–4% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is mixed (±0.33) and forecast is volatile, smooth transitions by averaging 2–3 consecutive days’ forecast values.  
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward bias correction of 1–2% per day until convergence.
